recentItems.title: Flash flood in the Himalayas: Thousands still missing a week after the disaster
recentItems.description:
A week on from a devastating flash flood in the Himalayas, nearly 4,500 people are still missing after a torrent of ice, rock and mud swept through parts of Nepal and China’s autonomous Tibet region, leaving a trail of destruction.

The disaster left behind at least 2.2 million tonnes of debris, according to the United Nations. International rescue teams are continuing their search for at least 600 hydropower plant workers trapped in tunnels in Nepal.

The death toll stands at more than 1,100 as rescue and recovery efforts continue across the affected areas. 

Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu reports live from Beijing with the latest from the Chinese government, while Tony Cheng joins live from Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu.

recentItems.title: Qatar condemns Iran's attacks on Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait
recentItems.description:
Qatar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has condemned Iran's attacks on Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait

A statement says: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs affirms that the continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that will complicate efforts aimed at containing tensions, undermine political and diplomatic endeavors aimed at achieving security and stability in the region and holds the Islamic Republic of Iran fully legally responsible for these attacks and all the repercussions and consequences resulting from them.

Al Jazeera’s Rob McBride joins live from Doha.

recentItems.title: 5,000 US sailors descend on Thailand as USS Abraham Lincoln docks
recentItems.description:
Thailand’s Pattaya is expecting a business boost as 5,000 US sailors arrive after spending nine months at sea aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln. The carrier supported the US war on Iran, while its record deployment was marked by deteriorating conditions on board.

recentItems.title: US-Venezuela oil agreement: Deal could help revive Venezuela's struggling economy
recentItems.description:
People in Venezuela are questioning whether the benefits from a controversial oil deal with the United States will actually go to them. The two countries recently announced an agreement that could bring in up to 100 billion dollars in investment in the next 25 years.

Al Jazeera’s Noris Soto reports from Caracas.

recentItems.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak: Calls for more safety measures as school year starts
recentItems.description:
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is causing concern for parents as the new school year starts. Some in Ituri province, one of the hardest hit areas, say schools are not prepared to protect children from the risk of infection.

Al Jazeera’s Alain Uaykani reports from Goma.

recentItems.title: SCO summit: China, Russia and Iran call for greater multilateral cooperation
recentItems.description:
25th anniversary at a summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, with calls for greater multilateral cooperation and a multipolar world order.

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian spoke against unilateralism and military blocs, while Russian President Vladimir Putin highlighted growing trade among SCO members.

Putin said trade between member states has risen above $400 billion, with national currencies playing a growing role in transactions.

The summit concluded with the SCO chairmanship passing to Pakistan, which is set to host the next meeting in Islamabad.

The report also briefly covers Israeli military activity in the occupied West Bank, including the use of tear gas at a mosque in Nablus.

recentItems.title: Nepalese community in UK mourns relatives lost in devastating Himalayan floods
recentItems.description:
Nepalese communities in the UK are holding vigils and prayer services for the victims of the devastating floods in the Himalayas, as many mourn relatives who are dead or missing. Promod Bhandari, who grew up in the badly affected village of Tupche, says he has lost dozens of family members and that his entire village has been washed away. Community leaders are co-ordinating support for bereaved families in Britain while raising funds for urgently needed aid in Nepal, even as some cope with missing relatives themselves. At a Hindu temple in London, members of the community gathered in prayer and candlelight vigils, expressing collective grief and solidarity with those affected by the disaster. 

Al Jazeer’s Camille Nedelec reports from Harlow, UK.
